entries.mechanism:
New York's broad-based categorical eligibility (SNAP 200-percent-class
state option; PolicyEngine models gross screen x1.3 FPL, x2 for
elderly/disabled households, at 2026-01 per gov/hhs/tanf/non_cash
parameters) is not in the composed us-ny/snap/fy-2026 program, which
applies only the standard federal tests. Every selected row is verified
per-row against axiom's persisted output surface: household gross income
sits inside the band above the federal 130 percent limit the composed
program applies and at or below the state's BBCE screen, verified
against axiom's own computed gross income and limit. Axiom-side modeling
boundary, tracked for encoding in rulespec-us#1098. The requested-month
regeneration preserves all five case identities and their boolean
left/right values exactly, so the evidence remains current.

Exact-household requested-month counterfactual on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The committed comparison adapter replayed over the same Case projection reproduces the report pin (Axiom 24.0 versus January PolicyEngine 69.39999389648438), and the unmodified direct requested-month simulation reproduces the same January value. Forcing the endogenously imputed allowable medical expenses (health insurance premiums and other medical expenses) to zero in the direct requested-month simulation produces January SNAP 23.84000015258789; its absolute delta from Axiom, 0.15999984741210938, is within the unchanged suite tolerance 7.0. Axiom receives zero medical-expense input while PolicyEngine imputes allowable medical expenses for the elderly/disabled member, feeding an excess medical deduction the bridge never projects to Axiom (axiom-oracles#362 class). Replay classifier record: class=medical.

Exact-household requested-month counterfactual on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The committed comparison adapter replayed over the same Case projection reproduces the report pin (Axiom 546.0 versus January PolicyEngine 489.8999938964844), and the unmodified direct requested-month simulation reproduces the same January value. Forcing the self-employment income inputs to zero in the direct requested-month simulation produces January SNAP 546.0; its absolute delta from Axiom, 0.0, is within the unchanged suite tolerance 7.0. Self-employment income enters the two engines on different surfaces (the projection's flat 0.6 netting versus PolicyEngine's state expense-based treatment), and zeroing it on the PolicyEngine side closes the residual. Replay classifier record: class=self_employment.

Exact-household requested-month replay on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The committed PolicyEngine value for this row reproduces bit-exact only through the comparison runner's single-case fallback path (PolicyEngineRunner.run_case -> policyengine household calculator: January SNAP 207.39999389648438 vs report pin 207.39999389648438); the batch dataset path — the suite's primary evaluation path, fed the identical Case inputs — returns a different January value, so the committed row reflects harness path divergence rather than an engine rule difference. The divergence is the fallback path's endogenous SSI imputation, absent from the batch input surface and from the Axiom projection: re-running the same fallback path with the SSI input forced to zero produces January SNAP 298.0, whose absolute delta from Axiom, 0.0, is within the unchanged suite tolerance 7.0. The engines priced different income surfaces (axiom-oracles#397 endogenous-income counterfactual family; a dedicated issue for the SSI imputation and for the batch-vs-fallback path inconsistency still needs filing).
